strings: Prepare for Battle marks the mobilization of the Peacekeepers as they assemble their forces to march out from town. Adventurers are called to make their final preparations and rendezvous with Valennia Stormfist in the Gustberry Lowlands before the company departs.

As regional tensions escalate, the local defense forces known as the Peacekeepers have sounded the call to arms. Troops and volunteers are ordered to secure their equipment, ready their weapons, and assemble for an organized march into the surrounding territory.

The staging area for the departing expedition is situated along the eastern road that heads north out of town into the Gustberry Lowlands. There, organizer Valennia Stormfist conducts a final inspection and roll call to ensure every fighter is fully prepared before the company marches into harm's way.

What Comes Next marks the culmination of affairs on Zephras Isle as travelers prepare to depart across the skies. With the local cult threat quelled and High Elder Shadowsong's blessing secured, skycutter transport is opened between the island and the plains of Mulgore.

With the local cult defeated and safety restored to Zephras Isle, High Elder Shadowsong has granted blessing for an onward journey. The island's expedition now looks beyond its shores, turning its focus across the open skies toward the continent of Kalimdor. Ayessa Dawnsinger coordinates the final departure for those ready to leave the island behind.

Establishing transport off the island required steady preparation. Muln worked diligently to secure stable skycutter travel between Zephras Isle and Mulgore. Following successful test voyages, an advance party has already crossed over to wait on the other side, preparing to make contact with the shaman of the Earthen Ring.

Across Teldrassil, a curious plant shimmers among the roots and canopy. Travelers bring a cutting to Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth, hoping the botanist can explain its origin.
In Teldrassil's boughs, a strange plant catches the light. Its fronds twist with a pulsing shimmer unlike the island's usual foliage. The glow draws the eye amid Teldrassil's young forest life.

At Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan recognizes the cutting as a plant from beyond northern Kalimdor. He last saw one decades ago, during a journey to the Swamp of Sorrows in the Eastern Kingdoms. How its seed crossed the ocean and grew so large on the World Tree puzzles him. Denalan begins cultivating the sample and testing it.
Where does the strange plant originally come from?
Denalan says the plant comes from the Swamp of Sorrows in the Eastern Kingdoms. He last saw a living specimen in those marshes decades ago.
frond origin | where is frond from | swamp plant
Denalan is a night elf botanist and herbalist near Lake Al'Ameth on Teldrassil. He studies and tends the island's growing plant life, experimenting with foreign seeds and planters.

No one knows how the plant reached Teldrassil. Denalan wonders how a seed crossed the Great Sea from the Eastern Kingdoms, then took root and grew large in Teldrassil's soil.

Denalan places the specimen in his planter at Lake Al'Ameth and begins testing it. Several fronds quickly sprout and blossom, giving him more to study.

The Strange Hermit is an introductory quest in Shadowgale Forest focusing on a shy, hooded recluse living away from civilization. Seeking conversation after long isolation, the hermit shares glimpses of his simple handcrafted life and his bond with the local singing forest spirits.

Deep within the secluded canopy of Shadowgale Forest lives an enigmatic, hooded recluse known simply as the Strange Hermit. Far removed from settled towns and standard trade routes, he spends his days in quiet isolation among the trees. When approached, his awkward speech and nervous demeanor show how long he has lived without ordinary companionship, making even a basic greeting an unfamiliar challenge.

Though solitary, the hermit insists he has all the company and provisions he needs. He confides that he once lived somewhere else before settling here, choosing to make a life surrounded by handmade trinkets and the local forest spirits. While the wild spirits frequently sing to him, he admits that melodic choruses cannot entirely replace speaking with someone who can truly answer back.

The strange hermit is an eccentric, hooded individual living in isolation within Shadowgale Forest. Unaccustomed to regular social interaction, he spends his time tending to handmade possessions and communing with local woodland spirits rather than other people.

The Forest's Bounty is a local quest in Shadowgale Forest where a timid forager asks for help collecting fallen acorns. Fierce predatory raptor-birds prowl the deeper woods, making harvesting too perilous without an adventurer's protection. The gathered acorns are then roasted into a tasty forest meal.

A cautious forager seeking food in Shadowgale Forest finds themselves in a bind. While acorns lie scattered across the woodland floor, the surrounding trees are prowled by fierce, raptor-like creatures. Having gathered whatever fell near safety, the forager depends on passing travelers to venture into the wilder groves so that neither goes hungry.

Shadowgale Acorns provide hearty sustenance for those who know how to prepare them. Though bitter or tough in the raw, roasting them over a crackling fire transforms the wild harvest into a rich, roasted treat. Braving the predatory birds among the timber turns a simple woodland scavenge into a warm meal shared in the wilderness.

Mercy Falls on Deaf Ears is a bounty offered by a grieving enclave seeking violent vengeance against the Al'Aketh cult. After suffering a terrible tragedy at the cultists' hands, the enclave promises coin and access to the Nightclaw's hidden lore in exchange for trophies harvested from their slain enemies. Taking up this task plunges travelers directly into the conflict spreading across Shadowgale Forest and surrounding territories.

The feud between the Nightclaw enclave and the Al'Aketh cultists is bitter and merciless. Following an unspecified but devastating tragedy inflicted upon the enclave, the survivors have abandoned any hope of peaceful reconciliation. To avenge their fallen kin, they turn to wandering adventurers and mercenaries, demanding violent retribution. In exchange for cutting down the cultists and taking their ears as grim proof of the deed, the enclave offers cold coin and the prospect of deeper trust.

The Al'Aketh operate across several wilderness areas, spreading their influence throughout the Gustberry Lowlands, the darkened woods of Shadowgale Forest, and the ancient Shrine of Akir. Their dark practices and fanatical nature have earned them the hatred of local inhabitants. By targeting their encampments across these territories, travelers not only weaken the cult's presence but also earn favor with the secretive Nightclaw, who guard their own esoteric mysteries closely until an outsider proves their loyalty.

Mercy Falls on Deaf Ears is a quest where an adventurer is hired to retaliate against the Al'Aketh cultists following a disastrous attack on a local enclave. The petitioner seeks retribution, requiring adventurers to slay cultists and return their severed ears as undeniable proof of the kill in exchange for coin and trust.
mercy falls on deaf ears quest | what is this quest | quest overview

Free the Hollows is a quest in Shadowgale Forest, where ghost-like spirits known as wind hollows linger among ancient ruins. Trapped by an ancient tragedy, their sorrowful singing haunts the surrounding woods until someone grants them release.

Elves dwelling across the island have long regarded Shadowgale Forest as a haunted grove, and their superstitions are grounded in truth. Deep within the woods to the northeast lie old stone ruins where phantom apparitions known as wind hollows drift endlessly among the overgrowth. Rather than hostile malice, these spirits project an air of deep sorrow, trapped by the weight of whatever disaster befell the ruins in ages past.

On quiet nights, travelers near the ruins report hearing a strange, ethereal singing drifting on the breeze. It does not resemble any known mortal song, carrying an intense melancholy that unsettles any who hear it. Believing that leaving these shades trapped in their eternal lament is a torment, compassionate travelers seek out the wind hollows to destroy their spectral bindings and grant them peace.

Wind hollows are sorrowful, ghost-like spirits that haunt old elven ruins to the northeast within Shadowgale Forest. Trapped by some ancient tragedy, they produce an eerie, mournful singing that echoes through the trees at night.

Tallonkai Swiftroot sends trusted champions into Fel Rock to stop Lord Melenas. The satyr has rallied the cave’s grell into an organized force, threatening night elf settlements near Teldrassil.

Satyrs recall an ancient betrayal that still stains kaldorei history. They were Highborne who gave themselves to the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients. Now one has made a foothold on Teldrassil, the young World Tree meant to be a sanctuary. For defenders like Tallonkai Swiftroot, that presence is a bitter disgrace.

Fel Rock lies north of the nearby paths, its corrupted caverns crawling with feral grell. Lord Melenas has gathered the chaotic creatures into a hostile force under his will. Tallonkai fears what the satyr may unleash on the World Tree’s boughs, and demands a swift, quiet end. He wants Melenas eliminated and his severed head brought back.
Lord Melenas is a satyr who has claimed Fel Rock in northern Teldrassil. He commands aggressive grell warriors and schemes to spread corruption through the World Tree.

Corithras Moonrage sends you to the Pools of Arlithrien for water as Gnarlpine furbolgs turn violent. His account of Teldrassil begins with Malfurion Stormrage's disappearance after the Third War.

Corithras Moonrage sends you with a tourmaline phial to a moonwell southeast of Darnassus's entrance, along the Pools of Arlithrien. The Gnarlpine furbolgs, once peaceful, now lash out with sudden violence. They ambush travelers and harry Sentinel patrols across the region. What seemed like isolated skirmishes has become a threat to the night elves' new home.

When you return with the filled phial, Corithras tells you how Teldrassil came to be. After the Third War, Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage vanished, leaving the Cenarion druids without a leader and divided. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm took the mantle of leadership in his absence. He urged the Circle of Ancients in Darkshore to set aside their mourning. The night elves, he argued, had to regain their lost immortality and heal their civilization by planting a vast new World Tree.

Crab Season is an urgent foraging task on Zephras centered on harvesting rare Windsong crawlers during their brief annual window. Because recent cultist activity has made the shores of Windsong Lake perilous, adventurers are called upon to brave both hostile interlopers and aggressive crustaceans.

On the shores of Windsong Lake across Zephras, a brief seasonal harvesting window opens for only a few weeks each year. The native Windsong crawlers emerge in numbers along the freshwater banks and tributary rivers, offering a rare harvest of meat to anyone bold enough to gather them before the annual opportunity slips away.

Recent surges in cultist activity around Zephras have disrupted daily life and endangered local foragers. With hostile cultists patrolling the wilderness, traveling to Windsong Lake has become far too hazardous for solitary gatherers, threatening to waste the fleeting crawler season unless capable adventurers step in to brave the shores and the ill-tempered crabs.

Windsong crawlers are a species of aggressive crab native exclusively to Windsong Lake on the island or land of Zephras. They are notable for being harvestable only during a brief seasonal window of a few weeks each year.

WANTED: Vulgara the Insatiable is a Peacekeeper bounty targeting a monstrous winged beast terrorizing the Shen'dar Highlands. Issued by Constable Aonda, the contract calls for adventurers to slay the ravenous vuldren and present her head to Danarii Bellowveil.

A formal bounty posted by Constable Aonda of the Peacekeepers marks Vulgara the Insatiable as an immediate danger to the highlands. The massive winged vuldren has terrorized travelers and local settlements from her roost southwest of Shen'dar Village, prompting local authorities to call on adventurous bounty hunters to bring her reign to an end.

This quest sends Alliance adventurers north along the coast of Darkshore to sift through the overgrown Ruins of Mathystra. Onu, an Ancient of Lore rooted in the Grove of the Ancients, seeks these ancient kaldorei artifacts to understand how the Twilight's Hammer cult is manipulating night elven sorcery for their sinister rites.

After adventurers recovered a tainted parchment from the cultists lurking around the colossal monument known as the Master's Glaive, Onu deciphered a disturbing revelation. Tainted by the Twilight's Hammer, the parchment revealed that these apocalyptic zealots are harnessing forgotten elven magic to awaken or summon their ancient masters back into the mortal world.

To counteract this dark endeavor, Onu directs heroes to the Ruins of Mathystra, located along the northeastern shores of Darkshore. Long ago, Mathystra was a shining bastion of highborne civilization before it shattered during the Sundering.
